description_en: Bhaṇḍārībādā is a village located 1 km north of Khalaṅgā (Jumla Bajār), the district headquarters of Jumla. Positioned on the edge of a hill ridge to the west of Bhaṇḍārībādā, the shrine is built adjacent to a stūpa (JUM0030). Both monuments are situated on a terrace along a small road leading to Simkhāḍā, north of Bhaṇḍārībādā.The shrine consists of a single square room with a door facing west. It stands on a 300 x 300 cm platform of square shape, featuring three steps of decreasing size. The walls are adorned with a central horizontal frieze containing two rows ofāmalakamotifs. The door is flanked by intricately carved pillars. Inside the room, at its center, there is a square pit. The ceiling is corbelled, with a central slab intricately decorated with a carved rosette. The monument is crowned by a roof comprising six plinths arranged in a maṇḍala (a square with a central projection, known as skt. bhadra) pattern, each plinth progressively smaller. Atop the final plinth rests a stūpa dome (skt.garbhagṛha).The shrine is referred to as a "cube-cell" by Prayag Raj Sharma (Sharma 1972, p. 91). Dilli Raj Sharma, on the other hand, describes it as a temple and erroneously mentions floral patterns carved on the doorjambs (Sharma 2012, pp. 188-189). Both authors failed to acknowledge the Buddhist nature of the shrine, indicated by the nearby stūpa and the stūpa crowning the shrine itself.The monument bears typological similarities to the stūpa located directly south of it (JUM0030), suggesting that they were likely built simultaneously. The dating of the stūpa itself is relatively easier. It resembles the stūpa at Kuchi Bihāra (ACH0010) and the one erected atop the Patharnauli reservoir (DLK0160). Both of these monuments were constructed in 1354 CE (ŚS 1276) by Devavarmā, the Great Minister (mahāmātya) of King Pṛthvīmalla. Therefore, it is plausible that both the stūpa and the shrine were built during the 14th century (Andolfatto 2019, pp. 96-97).
monument_assessment: Slightly damaged (minor damages such as minor cracks, plants, missing stones in plinths)
